name: Motor Assisted Bicycle
description: Ontario's moped: a bicycle of no more than 55 kg with pedals operable at all times and an electric motor, or one of 50 cc or less, without the power to reach more than 50 km/h; an e-bike past the power-assisted bicycle limits that stays within these lands here.

restrictions.rule: Pedals operable at all times to propel it, and weighs no more than 55 kg
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: An attached electric motor, or one of 50 cc or less, with no hand- or foot-operated clutch or gearbox
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: Without the power to reach more than 50 km/h on level ground within 2 km of a standing start; no limit on motor wattage
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: A motor vehicle, not a bicycle or power-assisted bicycle
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: Riders must be 16 or older with a class M licence
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 38(1); O. Reg. 340/94, s. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Passing the road tests on a moped or limited-speed motorcycle limits the licence to those (the L condition)
Must be registered and plated, and carry liability insurance
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 7(1); Compulsory Automobile Insurance Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.25, s. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Every rider must wear a motorcycle helmet with the chin strap fastened
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 104(1)
Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 178(3)

restrictions.rule: Not allowed on the 400-series highways, the Queen Elizabeth Way or the other controlled-access highways listed in Regulation 630
A municipality may ban it from its roads by by-law
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 185(2)

restrictions.rule: A dealer selling a new one must give the buyer a Ministry-approved document certifying it meets this definition
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 105(2)
